pending_commit.commit_message: shill: allow reusing the same IOHandlerFactory instance IOHandlerFactory exists mainly to allow the creation of IOHandler objects be mocked out by overridding IOHandlerFactory::CreateIO{Input,Ready}Handler(), and it doesn't carry any state. This CL turns IOHandlerFactory into something similar to Ares and Time, which allows reusing the same instance of IOHandlerFactory via IOHandlerFactory::GetInstance(). Follow-up CLs will migrate existing code to use IOHandlerFactory::GetInstance() instead of creating a new instance of IOHandlerFactory. BUG=None TEST=Run unit tests. dlcservice: change to a normal (long-lived) system daemon See BUG field for rationale behind the decision. Here is a summary of what this CL does: 1. Remove dbus activation file. 2. Simplify init conf file. 3. Remove RAII-style shutdown scheduler. 4. Update unittest. 5. Set respawn/respawn limit in init conf file. Also I removed redundant dbus constants defs in system_api. Rationale about respawn limit: dlcservice takes a bit more than 1 sec (1 test-dlc installed) to boot: localhost ~ # time minijail0 -u dlcservice -g dlcservice -G -n /usr/sbin/dlcservice --load_installed=true real 0m1.147s user 0m0.016s sys 0m0.023s localhost ~ # time minijail0 -u dlcservice -g dlcservice -G -n /usr/sbin/dlcservice --load_installed=false real 0m1.088s user 0m0.017s sys 0m0.014s respawn limit 3 10 is a popular setting in src/platform and it works fine for dlcservice - respawn takes less than 2 seconds and if respawning more than 3 times in 10 seconds probably means it is less likely to recover. When more/bigger DLCs are added later, this limit may have to be revisited but it's hard to predict at this moment. BUG=chromium:905071 TEST=unittest, platform.DLCService TEST=below ~#for i in {1..20}; do echo "Loop $i"; killall dlcservice; sleep 1; done Loop 1 Loop 2 Loop 3 Loop 4 Loop 5 dlcservice: no process found Loop 6 dlcservice: no process found Loop 7 dlcservice: no process found Cq-Depend: chromium:1602938,chromium:1602563 Change-Id: I2d860827c0da5631008e15d296ce0049946005cf Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1602894 Commit-Ready: Xiaochu Liu <xiaochu@chromium.org> Tested-by: Xiaochu Liu <xiaochu@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nicolas Norvez <norvez@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Amin Hassani <ahassani@chromium.org>

Factory shim is not stored as cros_payload, and it's not located at the last partition in an image, so we can only create a new shim image with old payloads and new factory shim to "replace" it. 2. When replacing release image, we might also want to replace the firmware as well. Add '--firmware_from_release' argument so that we don't need to use `image_tool get_firmware` to get the firmware from release image manually. UPSTREAM: mm, procfs: breakdown RSS for anon, shmem and file in /proc/pid/status There are several shortcomings with the accounting of shared memory (SysV shm, shared anonymous mapping, mapping of a tmpfs file). The values in /proc/<pid>/status and <...>/statm don't allow to distinguish between shmem memory and a shared mapping to a regular file, even though theirs implication on memory usage are quite different: during reclaim, file mapping can be dropped or written back on disk, while shmem needs a place in swap. Also, to distinguish the memory occupied by anonymous and file mappings, one has to read the /proc/pid/statm file, which has a field for the file mappings (again, including shmem) and total memory occupied by these mappings (i.e. equivalent to VmRSS in the <...>/status file. Getting the value for anonymous mappings only is thus not exactly user-friendly (the statm file is intended to be rather efficiently machine-readable). To address both of these shortcomings, this patch adds a breakdown of VmRSS in /proc/<pid>/status via new fields RssAnon, RssFile and RssShmem, making use of the previous preparatory patch. These fields tell the user the memory occupied by private anonymous pages, mapped regular files and shmem, respectively. Other existing fields in /status and /statm files are left without change. The /statm file can be extended in the future, if there's a need for that. CHROMIUM: devfreq: Fix rk3288_dmc / cpufreq interactions When I switched my device over to the "schedutil" governor and it was sitting on the sign in page (instead of the spinning login animation) I started seeing _tons_ of devfreq timeouts spamming my console. I did a tad bit of debugging and found that something about the way rk3288_dmcfreq was trying to lock the CPU Frequency just wasn't working. Specifically I printed the frequency of "pll_apll" when I was seeing a timeout and found that it was really low. Instead of debugging why the old way of doing things didn't work anymore, I decided to just switch rk3288_dmc to request a higher CPU Frequency by using the cpufreq notifiers. That's what everyone else does and is the supported way. It seems to work great. As a side effect of this it turns out that we can easily override the CPU Frequency that thermal throttling (and, actually, sysfs) imposed on the system. Thinking about this it actually seems like a beneficial thing to do. Sure we'll temporarily bump up to a really high CPU when we're hot, but we'll very quickly bump back down. ...and overall we may save power because we won't get so many failed transitions and we'll also spend less time with all CPUs spinning waiting for the transition to be done. Adding a test to one of the batches is as easy as adding a method to the class of the batch. This CL implement two batches - 'LE Sanity' and 'Stand Alone Sanity', and one package - 'BT Quick Sanity' that run both these batches. FROMGIT: ACPI: PM: Set enable_for_wake for wakeup GPEs during suspend-to-idle I noticed that recently multiple systems (chromebooks) couldn't wake from S0ix using LID or Keyboard after updating to a newer kernel. I bisected and it turned up commit f941d3e41da7 ("ACPI: EC / PM: Disable non-wakeup GPEs for suspend-to-idle"). I checked that the issue got fixed if that commit was reverted. I debugged and found that although PNP0C0D:00 (representing the LID) is wake capable and should wakeup the system per the code in acpi_wakeup_gpe_init() and in drivers/acpi/button.c: localhost /sys # cat /proc/acpi/wakeup Device S-state Status Sysfs node LID0 S4 *enabled platform:PNP0C0D:00 CREC S5 *disabled platform:GOOG0004:00 *disabled platform:cros-ec-dev.1.auto *disabled platform:cros-ec-accel.0 *disabled platform:cros-ec-accel.1 *disabled platform:cros-ec-gyro.0 *disabled platform:cros-ec-ring.0 *disabled platform:cros-usbpd-charger.2.auto *disabled platform:cros-usbpd-logger.3.auto D015 S3 *enabled i2c:i2c-ELAN0000:00 PENH S3 *enabled platform:PRP0001:00 XHCI S3 *enabled pci:0000:00:14.0 GLAN S4 *disabled WIFI S3 *disabled pci:0000:00:14.3 localhost /sys # On debugging, I found that its corresponding GPE is not being enabled. The particular GPE's "gpe_register_info->enable_for_wake" does not have any bits set when acpi_enable_all_wakeup_gpes() comes around to use it. I looked at code and could not find any other code path that should set the bits in "enable_for_wake" bitmask for the wake enabled devices for s2idle. [I do see that it happens for S3 in acpi_sleep_prepare()]. Thus I used the same call to enable the GPEs for wake enabled devices, and verified that this fixes the regression I was seeing on multiple of my devices.
